case.title: Undo brings back the shifts that a lead change cleared
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682427 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682427 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1} with one approved line, led by {Technician-A}. {Technician-B} is not the technician on that line.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682427 Undo Shifts and {Work-order-1} is S2-37451.
  • On the Schedule, {Technician-A} has two "Entire work order" shifts on {Work-order-1}: {Shift-A} today, which started an hour ago and ends later today, and {Shift-B} tomorrow.
    For example: {Shift-A} is today 9:00 to 15:00 and {Shift-B} is tomorrow 8:00 to 12:00.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  2. Click "Clear shifts".
  3. Click "Undo" on the message.
  4. Click "Schedule" in the top menu.
  5. Look at {Technician-A}'s row today.
  6. Go to tomorrow.
  7. Look at {Technician-A}'s row.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the question "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" opens, with "Keep shifts", "Clear shifts" and "Cancel".
  • Step 2: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 3: the message closes, {Work-order-1} goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button. No question about scheduled shifts appears.
  • Step 4: the Schedule opens on today.
  • Step 5: {Shift-A} is there with its original end time (for example 15:00), not cut short.
  • Step 6: the Schedule shows tomorrow.
  • Step 7: {Shift-B} is back, as it was (for example 8:00 to 12:00).

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. The cleared shifts stay cleared. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Please try again.” shows.”
  • S4-R29: “The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.”

Not yet checked against a build.

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11524)
